encodes: Why the format carries two separate keys: a salted commitment must never be compared against a raw nonce.
description: The sidecar carries the commitment value in the nonce key and the nonce value in the commitment key. Both are present, both are well-formed 32-byte values, and both belong to the same real payment, so a verifier that treats the two keys as interchangeable, or that falls back to one generic authorization field, will report LINKED. It must not. This is the failure the two-key split was introduced to prevent, and it is the one case a single-field implementation cannot see.
limits: The commitment and the nonce in this vector are from our own mainnet payment of 18 October 2026, so both are real values, not placeholders.
A verifier can also fail this on AUTHORIZATION_MISMATCH depending on which pair it compares first; either refusal is correct, reporting LINKED is not.
